what_this_proves: A scene can be created and modified over REST as well as by voice; its material, light colour and camera lens are set and read back; it can be animated with keyframes read back from Blender's F-curves; it can be exported to GLB/FBX with each file verified in place by the device; and the render and every file path now satisfy the device's own checks, which the shipped driver and the Cloud Core did not before.

measured_first.before: app/creative3d after M25: voice-only creation, no REST create/apply; set_material colour/metallic/roughness written but only colour read back; set_light energy only; set_camera look_at only; no animation; no export (the corpus kept 'Sahneyi dışa aktar.' as a negative); 0 production scenes.
measured_first.contract_defects: blender_driver.do_render declared 'path': <absolute path> (SceneInspection.Confine refuses it: permission_denied); SceneService._inspect_device read payload['render_png_base64'] while ProjectCapabilities.Inspect answers render.png_base64; tests/creative3d_support.FakeCreative3DDevice answered the Cloud Core's shape, and SceneLab.DriverScript (not the shipped driver) was what the device lab ran; scripts/tests/blender-scene-lab.py checked demo.blend after the driver began saving scene.blend.

found_on_the_way.absolute_render_path: the shipped driver's render path was absolute; the device has always refused absolute paths inside out.json, so every real render through the Cloud Core would have ended in permission_denied.
found_on_the_way.render_key: the Cloud Core read render_png_base64; the device sends render.png_base64. Only the fake sent the former.
found_on_the_way.fake_kinder_than_the_device: the fake device returned whatever path the driver wrote and a top-level base64 key, so neither defect could fail a Python test; it now answers and refuses like SceneInspection, and its keys are pinned to the C# source.
found_on_the_way.lab_ran_its_own_driver: the device lab's real-Blender test drove SceneLab.DriverScript; the new SceneExportTests test drives the repository's blender_driver.py.
found_on_the_way.lab_script_stale_blend: scripts/tests/blender-scene-lab.py looked for demo.blend; the driver saves scene.blend since M25's service-command lab.
found_on_the_way.light_on_a_camera: apply_light accepted any object with data; a camera has data too, and setting energy on it was an AttributeError reported as a vague error; lights are now known by type.
found_on_the_way.export_proof_overwritten: each inspection replaced the scene row's exports with the current run's, so exporting FBX erased the verified proof of the GLB still on the owner's disk; proofs now merge by format (a re-proven format replaces its own entry).
found_on_the_way.animated_pose: after keyframes are inserted the object holds its LAST keyframe's value; the driver now evaluates the scene at its first frame so the read-back is the scene's opening pose.

tests.services/api/tests/unit/test_creative3d_: spec bounds + Blender-only refusals; driver read-back of every new control (relative render, first-frame pose, lens, light colour, material, frames, F-curve keys, GLB export signature); FBX magic and light-by-type; compare names every drift (frames, keyframe value, frame range, lens, light colour, metallic, unverified export, lying hash); fake device refusals; fake keys == C# Inspect keys; service end to end (render stored, exports_json, FBX re-export); router words; voice animate + export (owner's word wins); clarification before any device call; tools tiered; REST create/apply/422/404

red_first_proof.method: Executed mutations restored from sha256-verified copies (never git checkout); scratchpad b44_mutate.py.
mutations: M1 the driver declares its render with an absolute path the device refuses (521) -> 1 failure(s).
M2 the Cloud Core reads the render from a key only the fake ever sent (521) -> 1 failure(s).
M3 an animated scene is left at its last keyframe instead of its first frame (526) -> 1 failure(s).
M4 the comparison never checks WHICH frames carry the keys (526) -> 1 failure(s).
M5 an export the device hashed differently from the driver still passes (527) -> 1 failure(s).
M6 the read-back never looks inside a layered action, so no keyframe is reported (526) -> 1 failure(s).
M7 a Unity plan may name an operation only the Blender driver implements (526/527) -> 1 failure(s).
M8 'Küreye bir animasyon ekle' becomes a new sphere (the animate match never runs first) (526) -> 1 failure(s).
M9 the creative export takes 'Bunu GLB olarak dışa aktar' from the scene (527) -> 1 failure(s).
M10 the model's format argument overrides the owner's own format word (527) -> 1 failure(s).
M11 a later export erases the verified proof of an earlier one (527) -> 1 failure(s).
M12 the Cloud Core drops the device's 'verified' word, so no export is ever proven (527) -> 1 failure(s).
red_first_proof.result: 12/12 red; every file restored to its sha256 before the mutation.
